Shaun eats here daily.How to make it200g jasmine rice2 L chicken stock1 5cm piece ginger, sliced2 chicken breasts3 spring onions, sliced2 tbsp soy sauce1 tsp sesame oil4 tbsp crispy fried shallotsRinse the rice and put in a big pot with the stock and ginger.Bring to the boil, then simmer gently, stirring often, until thick and creamy.Poach the chicken breasts in the congee, then shred.Ladle into bowls and top with chicken, spring onion, soy, sesame oil and fried shallots.Bus fight sticky pork baoHoisin honey roast pork in steamed buns with cucumber, spring onion and peanutsHow to make it800g pork scotch fillet4 tbsp hoisin sauce2 tbsp honey2 tbsp soy sauce2 garlic cloves, crushed12 frozen bao buns1 Lebanese cucumber, cut into sticks3 spring onions, sliced50g roasted peanuts, crushedMix the hoisin, honey, soy and garlic and coat the pork.Marinate in the fridge.Roast at 200°C, basting with the marinade twice, until sticky and charred.Rest and slice thinly, and steam the bao buns.Fill with pork, cucumber, spring onion and peanuts.Macau pork and prawn dumplingsThe fight club up the side of a Macau towerHow to make itAs written, serves 4Pork and prawn dumplings with ginger and spring onion, steamed in bamboo baskets and served with chilli oil and black vinegar.Mix 300g pork mince with 200g finely chopped peeled prawns, 1 tbsp grated ginger, 2 sliced spring onions, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tsp sesame oil and a pinch of white pepper.Put a heaped teaspoon on each of 30 round dumpling wrappers, wet the edges and pleat closed.Steam in a paper-lined bamboo basket over boiling water for 8 minutes.Serve with chilli oil and black vinegar.Spring onion pancakes with chilli oilKaty's Hotel California, slightly off key.How to make itA house standard, not part flesh is opaque at the bone.Cook the rice and steam the bok choy.Top the fish with fresh spring onion, pour over the soy, then smoking hot oil.Valet night beef and broccoli noodlesValet Katy, with a Berkeley honours degreeHow to make itAs written, serves 4Beef strips seared hot in a wok with garlic and broccoli, tossed with egg noodles and oyster sauce until glossy, served in takeaway boxes.Slice 500g rump thinly and toss with 1 tbsp soy and 1 tsp cornflour.Soak 400g egg noodles as the pack says.Sear the beef in a very hot wok with oil in 2 batches and remove.Stir-fry 1 head broccoli in florets and 3 sliced garlic cloves for 2 minutes with a splash of water.Add the noodles, beef, 4 tbsp oyster sauce and 1 tbsp soy and toss until glossy.SweetsDragon scale mango puddingSilky mango and
